content_text: Shell Pilipinas continues to grow earnings and maintain rigorous capital discipline that underpins long-term value, even amid macroeconomic challenges. With a focus on performance, discipline and simplification, we are steadily enhancing our ability to deliver consistent results and unlock our full potential. Strategic investments in operational excellence, supply security and customer-centric solutions have strengthened our business. We have maintained high premium fuel leadership with Shell V-Power and achieved robust lubricants growth with Shell Helix and Shell Advance. Moreover, our expanded non-fuel offerings - including Shell Café, auto workshops, and digital marketing initiatives in our lubricants and mobility segments - have elevated customer experiences and driven growth. The inauguration of our fourth import terminal in South Mindanao in 2025 will further secure our supply and meet rising demand.

Innovation is the cornerstone of our balanced growth. Since 2016, Shell Pilipinas has reduced Scope 1 and Scope 2 carbon emissions by over 90% and introduced sustainable, lower-carbon solutions such as Shell Bitumen FreshAir, Carbon Neutral Lubricants and Shell Recharge stations. These early-stage initiatives underscore our commitment to being a responsible energy provider. Through the Pilipinas Shell Foundation Inc., we actively advance national development by promoting the UN Sustainable Development Goals. Our initiatives in education, livelihood, health, food security, environmental stewardship, and energy access are making a lasting impact on the communities we serve. Driven by a relentless pursuit of excellence, we are transforming our downstream business to deliver more value with less emissions while focusing on areas of competitive strength.

With an emphasis on safety, people and sustainability, we achieved employee engagement and diversity & inclusion scores of 81% and 86% respectively in our latest Shell People Survey, placing us in the top quartile. Our commitment is further recognised by our second consecutive Diversity Company Circle of Excellence award at the CEO Asia Awards, reaffirming Shell Pilipinas as an employer of choice. Our success is built on a robust performance culture and a unified team working toward a common vision.

Driven by a relentless pursuit of excellence, we are transforming our downstream business to deliver more value with less emissions while focusing on areas of competitive strength. Shell Pilipinas is dedicated to creating lasting value as the preferred energy partner and the most customer-focused energy marketer. Together, we will forge ahead to shape a better future in the Philippines. Min Yih Tan Chairman of the Board

Shell Pilipinas Corporation represents the downstream operations of Shell companies in the Philippines (SciP) engaged in oil importation, distribution, marketing, energy trading, and other services. Shell Pilipinas operates an integrated supply chain and mobility network composed of 24 fuel terminals and supply points, 10 lubricant warehouses, two bitumen facilities, and three import facilities. The Company supports a network of more than 1,100 service stations in addition to industrial and commercial customers. The Company imports and markets a range of petroleum products, such as gasoline, diesel, jet fuel, fuel oil, lubricants, and bitumen. In addition, it provides non-fuel retail products and services through Shell Select convenience stores, Shell deli2go outlets, Shell Cafés, and vehicle service centres nationwide. SciP is part of Shell plc, a global group of energy and petrochemical companies operating in over 70 countries. Find out more about Shell Pilipinas at www.pilipinas.shell.com.ph.

3-3, 2-1 Shell Pilipinas traces its roots back to Asiatic Petroleum Company (Philippine Islands) Ltd., an importer and retailer of motor gasoline and kerosene. The organisation underwent several structural and name changes, becoming Pilipinas Shell Petroleum Corporation in 1973. The Company's corporate name was changed to Shell Pilipinas Corporation (SPC) in 2023 to reflect its adaptive business strategy and progressive sustainability priorities, as the Company aims to deliver services beyond petroleum. The Tabangao Refinery began its commercial operations in 1962, with an initial nameplate capacity of 30,000 barrels per day (bpd). Modernisation and expansion activities between 1993 and 1995 further increased the oil refinery's nameplate capacity to 110,000 bpd. It was one of only two oil refineries in the Philippines. In 2020, the Company permanently ceased its refining operations and shifted into a fullimport supply chain model. The Company transformed its Tabangao Refinery into a 100% import terminal aptly called Shell Import Facility-Tabangao, or SHIFT. The new supply strategy is supported with two other import terminals-one in northern Luzon and one in northern Mindanao. A fourth import terminal in southern Mindanao will be opened in 2025. Today, Shell Pilipinas continues to be one of the most recognisable, trusted, and preferred brands in the country, serving thousands of motorists every day through its network of over 1,100 service stations nationwide. 1914 to 1954

content_text: 3-3, 207-1, 207-2 As an importer, Shell Pilipinas remains exposed to foreign exchange fluctuations. The Company manages this risk through strategic importation planning and consideration of projected exchange rate movements. The Board of Directors, through the Board Audit and Risk Oversight Committee, oversees financial reporting, including the evaluation and approval of financial statements. In compliance with the Philippine Standards on Auditing, an independent auditor, as approved by shareholders, provides an opinion on the fairness of the audited financial statements. To reinforce accountability, business managers certify Business Assurance Letters annually, confirming compliance and integrity. The President and CEO, along with the Corporate Audit and Assurance Manager, certify the adequacy and effectiveness of internal controls. Based on these assurances, the Board Audit and Risk Oversight Committee assesses the effectiveness of Shell Pilipinas' governance, risk management, and control processes. Since 2022, the Company ensures high quality in its internal audit functions from Corporate Assurance and Audit Department (CAAD) as aligned with the Code of Ethics for Internal Audit Practitioners and International Standards for the Professional Practice of Internal Auditing.

Shell Pilipinas is committed to distributing annual dividends of at least 75% of its previous year's audited net income, subject to legal requirements and Board approval. The Board regularly reviews dividend amounts based on the company's earnings, financial health, cash flow, capital needs, and other relevant factors to ensure a sound and sustainable operation. Ultimately, the Board has sole discretion in determining the amount, type, and timing of dividend payments. Future dividends will depend on the company's financial performance, investment plans, and cash flow. Additionally, foreign shareholders can only remit dividends using Philippine bank-sourced foreign exchange if their investment was registered with the Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas and covered by the required Bangko Sentral Registration Document. Driving financial resilience has been a resounding theme in our journey for 2024. While it has been a year of unprecedented challenges, it is most importantly a year of reaffirming our purpose-powering progress together with the Filipino. With a strong resolve to make SPC the investment case, we delivered 15% growth in core earnings, Php 900 Mn of OPEX savings and avoidance, and Php 2.8 Bn reduction in CAPEX.

During our midpoint strategy refresh, we communicated the following 2023-25 strategic priorities: 1) Strong earnings, cash, and dividend-paying positions, 2) A major player in the energy industry, and 3) Setting the bar on governance and energy transition. Standing on these priorities, Shell Pilipinas increased net income to Php 1.3 Bn in 2024 despite elevated interest rate, oil price volatility, and stronger USD.

The petroleum market remains to be hypercompetitive. Our total volume declined by 3% in 2024, lowering the double-digit gap at the beginning of the year. Despite this, core earnings improved to Php 2.6 Bn with margin uplift from higher premium product penetration, new customer wins, and prudent cost management. Our Commercial businesses expanded volume and earnings throughout 2024. Commercial Fuels maintained its sector leadership in Power, Manufacturing, Mining and Marine - growing total volumes by 3%. In addition, higher demand for FuelSave Diesel and FuelOil Plus boosted premium sales vs. 2023. Lubricants grew volumes by 10% as the business successfully rolled out its new routeto-market strategy, gained new customers, and raised Shell Advance to its highest volume performance. Likewise, Aviation and Construction & Road businesses have consistently grown earnings year after year. In Mobility, our Non-Fuel Retail (NFR) continues to be a growth engine, delivering double-digit profit growth for four consecutive years. Effective marketing promotions boosted Car Care and Lubricants sales throughout the year. Other NFR segments such as Convenience Retail (CR) and Alliance also grew by 28% and 3%, respectively. Beyond the topline improvement, Shell Pilipinas ramped up supply chain optimisation and structural cost reduction efforts. Total OPEX savings and interest avoidance in 2024 surpassed target by 80%. The embedding of Shell Performance Framework across the organisation enables us to change our business model, right-size our assets, and prioritise spend that gives the best bang for the buck.

Cash Flow from Operations (CFFO) continues to improve, closing 2024 at Php 7 .5 Bn, up from Php 4.3 Bn last year. This is the highest CFFO delivered by SPC since 2018 and was achieved through earnings growth, sustained capital discipline, and optimised inventory levels. In 2024, CAPEX was reduced to Php 2.1 Bn, from Php 4.9 Bn in 2023. While we continue to invest in Mobility and Supply Chain, investment decisions go through a more stringent process to find more cost-effective ways in building new or upgrading existing assets. This includes value engineering, scope optimisation, and more economical sourcing strategies. In addition, we continue to high-grade our portfolio of assets. The Mobility business closed 53 non-performing sites in 2024 to prevent further losses and generate savings from site operating costs. This also enables us to re-channel resources to sites where we are more competitive and can deliver better returns. Strong focus in managing working capital remained, matching the timing of collections with payables and optimising inventory levels. However, prepaid taxes have increased by Php 1.9 Bn reflecting the unutilized Creditable Withholding Tax (CWT) certificates in 2024. While the balance can be used against future income tax payable, we need to produce higher earnings to accelerate the depletion of these prepaid assets. Despite the substantial improvement against last year, Free Cash Flow (FCF) still ended at Php 1.6 Bn deficit. The management will accelerate its efforts to deliver positive FCF and strengthen the balance sheet.

With improved earnings performance, the company's Retained Earnings Available for Dividend Declaration by the end 2024 has increased to Php 1.4 Bn from Php 246 Mn in 2023. This puts us at a better position to distribute earnings to our shareholders. However, with the deficit in FCF, the company's gearing level remains elevated at 56%. The company needs to prioritise deleveraging and reduce borrowing costs which have been substantially higher in the past three years. We recognise the urgency, and more drastic measures will be undertaken as part of our 2025-30 strategy. The company remains committed in rewarding our shareholders with attractive dividend payment as per our policy. The management is working towards achieving positive FCF and reduce gearing to 50% or lower, in order to resume dividend payout at the earliest possible time.

content_text: 110 Years of Progress with New Shell FuelSave Shell Pilipinas celebrated 110 years of empowering Filipino journeys by launching its latest Shell FuelSave formulation, reinforcing its commitment to sustainable and efficient mobility. Held at the Clark International Speedway in Pampanga, the event brought together 110 motorists to experience the 'Sulit ang Bawat Trip' promise. Attendees witnessed the eco-friendly benefits of the upgraded Shell FuelSave, which is designed to improve fuel economy, enabling drivers to save up to one litre per full tank or extend their trips by up to 15 kilometres-delivering both fuel economy and reduced environmental impact. The launch of Shell FuelSave marks a milestone in Shell's drive toward sustainability, which completes its most efficient fuel portfolio to date alongside last year's introduction of the new Shell V-Power. As part of Shell's 110th anniversary celebrations, this initiative highlights the Company's enduring commitment to innovation and its role in shaping a more sustainable future for Filipino motorists.

In an increasingly fast-paced market, Shell Pilipinas sharpens its focus on optimising resources, cutting operational costs, and maximising returns on every investment to drive shareholder value, sustainable growth, and operational excellence to strengthen the business and advance Shell's sustainability agenda.

Since implementing a hybrid work model in November 2022, Shell Manila Office has successfully optimised its operations while promoting sustainability. With employees working onsite two to three times per week and an average turnout of 40% between April and June 2024, the office consolidated its operations, surrendering one floor of office space. This move is projected to deliver significant savings in rent and facilities management cost through 2028, while reducing annual carbon emissions. By October 2024, office space utilisation rose to 60%. In a collaborative effort, over 130 boxes used during the transition were repurposed into a Christmas tree by the Shell National Students Art Competition (NSAC) artists, which symbolises creativity and shared values. This exemplifies Shell's commitment to operational efficiency, sustainability, and fostering a resourceful and productive work environment.

Optimising Land Lease Agreements for Greater Value Shell Pilipinas has made significant strides in optimising its land lease footprint as part of its regular reviews. A key success was the renegotiation of the Prime Energy Malampaya Onshore Gas Plant (MOGP) Lease and Right-of-Way (ROW) agreement in Tabangao, Batangas. With the 25-year lease set to expire in August 2024, SPC secured a new 15-year deal. This substantial gain strengthens SPC's financial position and supports the competitiveness of its marketing segments.

3-3 Shell Pilipinas continued its strong growth trajectory in 2024 through Lubricants' products and services portfolio-by both retail and technical solutions. Notably, the Company secured regulatory approval to extend its lubricant services beyond its existing customer base.

Shell Philippines Gets SEC Approval to Expand Lubricants Services On December 16, 2024, Shell Pilipinas Corporation secured approval from the Philippines Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) to expand its lubricant services. The Company can now extend technical services associated with its lubricant business to a wider customer base, including those who do not currently purchase its products, thereby creating additional revenue opportunities. The stand-alone Shell Lubricants Technical Services offering aims to position the business as a pioneering end-to-end solutions service provider whilst providing an additional revenue stream for Shell Lubricants. With stand-alone Technical Services guided by Shell's expert Technical Advisers, Shell Lubricants can now independently provide solutions such as Shell LubeAnalyst, an oil condition monitoring service, and Shell LubeOptimiser, an advanced lubrication management service, along with other expert lubrication advice to a broader customer base, thereby enhancing operational efficiency. For more information about Shell Lubricants Technical Services, go to: https://www.shell.com/businesscustomers/lubricants-for-business/lubricantsservices.html Brewing Bold Success with Shell Café in 2024 Since its 2023 debut, Shell Café has sustained remarkable momentum in offering high-quality coffee and food that connect with local tastes. In 2024, the brand cemented its position as a key driver of growth for SPC, achieving significant milestones in expansion, sales, and customer engagement. With a vision to become the go-to spot for coffee, pastries, and meals, Shell Café introduced its Signature and Espresso coffee blends alongside a curated menu of sweet and savoury pastries, rice meals, and sausage frankfurters. By the end of 2024, Shell Café operated 60 branches, including new outlets and shop conversions across Luzon, Visayas, and Mindanao. The results speak volumes about Shell Cafe's success. Its coffee category became the fastest-growing segment in Shell Select, with high double-digit growth of average coffee cups sold per day vs. previous year. Food service contribution to the Select business was also at an all-time high. An organic social media post that went viral in February 2024 followed by high engagements from influencers and food community groups further boosted visibility and performance, doubling coffee cup sales during this peak period and generating significant earned media mileage. The Philippines category management team was also recognised as the Best in Food Service among the Shell Mobility markets in Asia, underscoring the brand's strategic launch and execution.

In 2024, Shell Pilipinas conducted a successful Line of Defense 2: Distribution Operations Review (DOR), reaffirming its dedication to operational excellence and compliance. This comprehensive review evaluated terminal distribution activities, assessed risk management practices, and uncovered opportunities to enhance business controls and performance. Since the last DOR in 2018, SPC's terminals and functional teams have prioritised strengthening operational safeguards, elevating staff competence, refining procedures, and establishing Performance Quality (PQ) testing facilities. These efforts bore fruit, along with the 2024 review earning high praise from global evaluators. The reviewers commended the local teams for their openness, curiosity, and commitment to continuous improvement, highlighting the absence of any serious or high-risk findings.

Shell Lubricants receives Best Customer Satisfaction Scores in Six years In 2024, Shell Lubricants achieved its highest Customer Satisfaction Index (CSI) score since 2019, reaching 8.8. content_text: Shell's commitment to sustainability and the energy transition was demonstrated through two significant initiatives in 2024: capacity-building programmes for employees and leaders, and a family-focused sustainability event. These efforts highlight Shell's dedication to fostering a culture of learning and environmental stewardship within its organisation and the broader community. Shell's approach to sustainability is rooted in educating its workforce while inspiring families and communities to embrace practices that contribute to a resilient and sustainable world.

For this reporting year, Shell Pilipinas enhanced its commitment to sustainability through targeted capacity-building programmes, equipping leaders and employees with the skills and knowledge necessary to drive the energy transition. These initiatives aligned with Shell's Powering Progress strategy, fostering a deeper understanding of critical environment, societal, and governance (ESG) topics and their practical integration into daily operations. The Carbon 101 training, attended by internal leaders and Board members, focused on the evolving carbon market, providing insights into carbon trading and Shell's role in global decarbonisation efforts. Similarly, the Water 101 session emphasised the water-climate nexus, highlighting sustainable water management and nature-based solutions to address environmental challenges. Shell also introduced the Electric Vehicle Fundamentals training, preparing employees for shifts in the transportation sector as electric vehicles (EV) gain prominence across the region. These programmes reflect Shell's proactive approach to equipping its workforce with the competencies needed to advance sustainability, address ESG priorities, and strengthen the Company's position as a leader in the energy transition.

3-3 Shell is making significant contributions to the Philippines' sustainable power alternatives, notably by expanding its EV charging network to become a net-zero energy business by 2050. Shell is dedicated to driving the shift towards a greener future for Filipino drivers.

Being true to its purpose to power progress by providing more and cleaner energy solutions and aligned to its mission to make life's journeys better, SPC has expanded its EV Charging Network with the launch of mall-based Shell Recharge stations in Metro Manila. content_text: Shell Instapave Drives Nationwide Strategy In 2024, Shell Instapave shows remarkable growth through Project ICE (Instapave Contractor Expansion), fueled by the appointment of Yoko Konstruk Corporation as the National Implementor for Shell Instapave technology. This strategic initiative led to a significant increase in demand compared to 2023, driven by a focused approach to saturate the base demand in Northern Luzon while establishing a foothold in South Luzon, Palawan, and the Visayas. A pivotal milestone was reached on February 16, 2024, when the DPWH Bureau of Construction released the Standard Detailed Unit Price Analysis (DUPA) for Item 304A. This standardisation ensured uniform cost derivation across implementing offices, paving the way for broader nationwide adoption of Shell Instapave. Shell Instapave, a cold-mix road surface treatment specified under DPWH Item 304A, requires no heating, offering a sustainable and efficient solution for infrastructure projects. With more than 60% year-on-year growth in 2024 and the critical support of the DPWH DUPA, Shell Instapave underscores the Company's commitment to delivering environmentally friendly, innovative infrastructure solutions across the Philippines.

Shell Pilipinas has teamed up with Flash Express, one of the Philippines' fastest-growing delivery service providers, to drive sustainability in the logistics sector through the Accelerate to Zero (A2Z) initiative. This partnership leverages Shell's advanced Application Programming Interfaces (API) to track the carbon footprint of Flash Express' extensive delivery network, enabling actionable strategies to reduce emissions. As the logistics sector in the Philippines continues its rapid growth, environmental challenges have come to the forefront. While motorcycles dominate the delivery landscape with relatively low emissions per vehicle, inefficiencies such as low-load trips over short distances contribute significantly to the sector's carbon impact. Through tools like carbon offset programmes and a forthcoming telematics system, Shell Fleet Solutions equip Flash Express to address these inefficiencies and make meaningful progress toward decarbonisation, setting a benchmark for sustainable logistics in the region.

content_text: In 2024, Shell Fleet Solutions partnered with global telematics leader Cartrack to transform fleet data analytics for businesses in the Philippines. This collaboration integrates Shell's fuel management expertise with Cartrack's advanced vehicle telematics, providing businesses with a unified platform for real-time insights into driver performance, vehicle operations, and automated fuel analytics. By streamlining data collection and analysis, the partnership empowers businesses to optimise fleet management, reduce costs, and enhance operational efficiency. The integration of Shell Card transaction data with Cartrack's telematics through the Shell Fleet Insights package simplifies fleet oversight while enabling measures to prevent fuel fraud, ensure compliance, and improve safety by monitoring driver behaviour. Beyond efficiency, the partnership supports sustainability goals, aligning with Shell's A2Z initiative to reduce fleet emissions. With nearly 2 Mn subscribers globally, Cartrack's expertise amplifies Shell Fleet Solutions' ability to provide data-driven tools that help businesses meet operational objectives while driving progress toward decarbonisation.

Shell Pilipinas recognises that achieving the energy transition starts with decarbonising its own operations. Over the years, the Company has made substantial investments and operational changes to becoming a net-zero energy company in the future.

The Company's import facilities and terminals have transitioned to using 100% LED lighting. To further reduce plastic usage, conventional hand soaps have been replaced with Suds Sustainable Pods. Dried leaves and food scraps are now repurposed to naturally fertilise small gardens, with the harvested vegetables distributed to contractors and employees. Additionally, dry leaves are collected and placed in compost pits, with a total of 492 bags hauled. By reducing air conditioning usage by 50%, from 24/7 to 12 hours each workday, the Company has achieved significant annual savings in electricity costs, while also reducing carbon emissions equivalent to planting more than 4,900 trees.

Shell Pilipinas has made significant strides in reducing the carbon footprint of its mobility operations. The installation of LED lights has been completed across all 500 sites, contributing to enhanced energy efficiency. In addition, solar panels have been installed at 176 of the targeted 200 sites, furthering the Company's commitment to renewable energy. Ecobricks have been integrated into 110 out of the targeted 120 sites, and 115 sites now feature green wall installations, promoting biodiversity and enhancing the aesthetic appeal of the locations. Furthermore, all sites have been painted with eco-friendly, non-harmful paints, ensuring that sustainability is integrated into every aspect of the operations.

As part of its sustainability goals, Shell Pilipinas has integrated renewable energy solutions into its operations, installing approximately 5,200 solar panels across terminal facilities to reduce reliance on conventional energy sources. An additional 300 solar panels have been deployed at bitumen facilities to support greener operations. Key locations, including the SHIFT, SLEX Mamplasan, and NLEX Bulacan Mobility sites, now fully operate on renewable power, underscoring the Company's commitment to reducing carbon emissions and advancing a sustainable future. Shell Pilipinas is committed to safeguarding the environment through proactive efforts to protect biodiversity, prevent oil spills, manage natural resources sustainably, and reduce emissions from operations and customer-supplied products. The Company actively pursues circular economy solutions to minimise waste from its facilities, complemented by investments in sustainable infrastructure and an increasing reliance on renewable energy to power its operations, mobility sites, and offices.

At Shell Pilipinas, making the most of resources is a key part of how we approach sustainability. It reflects our commitment to protecting the environment and managing resources responsibly. With the growing need for businesses to reduce their impact on the planet, we take a proactive approach to improving efficiency, conserving resources, and embracing circularity in our operations.

Shell Pilipinas continues to be a key participant in Shell's Carbon-Neutral Programme, the largest initiative of its kind in the global lubricants industry. In 2024, Shell Pilipinas sold carbon-neutral oils including Shell Helix, Gadus, Tellus, Omala, and Corena brands amounting to 940 tonnes equivalent CO2e carbon reduction offset equivalent to planting 15,000 trees. On top of this, SPC continues to comply with the Extended Producer's Responsibility (EPR) Law of 2022, requiring manufacturers to manage the disposal and recycling of their plastic packaging. Shell Lubricants has managed to procure 480 tonnes of plastic credits in compliance with the EPR Law. Furthering its circularity efforts, Shell Lubricants also continues to collect plastics from the market and its operations via its Shell LubeRecycle and Shell Plasticycle programmes, amounting to over 5.4 tonnes of plastic collected to date. Shell Pilipinas' efforts in continuing to support the industry's carbon-neutral initiatives enable the sector as well as the consumers to move to a more sustainable future.

content_text: Efficient water management is central to our sustainability efforts, as we recognise the critical importance of safeguarding this essential resource. SPC employs innovative technologies and practices to reduce water consumption and reduce reliance on freshwater sources, helping to mitigate the potential environmental impact of water use.

3-3, 303-1, 303-2 Water is one of the most vital resources for sustaining life. Shell Pilipinas continuously works to minimise its water consumption while enhancing water reuse and recycling across its operations. At its terminals, rainwater is collected through drain canals, is filtered onsite using an oil-water separator. This process ensures that any oil-contaminated water is treated before being released, preventing environmental harm. Effluents from operations are regularly monitored and sampled in accordance with standards set in Shell's HSSE & SP Control Framework. The Company complies with effluent regulations, including those outlined in the Department of Environment and Natural Resources (DENR) Administrative Order (DAO) 34 and 35, the DAO 2016-08, the Clean Water Act, and the Global Energy Monitor. Effluent samples are tested by a DENR-accredited third-party laboratory. To reduce freshwater consumption, SHIFT is one of the terminals contributing to the Company's global goal of a 15% reduction in freshwater use by 2025. Although four major facilities are in areas facing high water stress, the Company has developed comprehensive water management plans to mitigate its impact.

content_text: The Company understands that the health of our planet's biodiversity is essential for resilient ecosystems and thriving communities. Ecosystems also play a key role in absorbing and storing carbon, making them critical in the fight against climate change. Aware of the potential risks of oil spills, Shell Pilipinas takes proactive steps to protect marine and terrestrial ecosystems with comprehensive oil spill mitigation strategies. Through various initiatives, we are committed to safeguarding natural resources and preserving the environment that supports life on Earth.

3-3, 304-2 Shell Pilipinas aims to have a positive impact on biodiversity wherever it operates. The Company adheres to stringent standards that minimise the potential environmental impacts of its operations, particularly in sensitive areas rich in biodiversity or designated as protected habitats. In collaboration with local government units, Shell Pilipinas actively participates in initiatives such as SHIFT and NMIF to assess and mitigate any potential impacts on local plants and animal species, as well as on natural ecosystems. The Company has an oil spill contingency plan in place to mitigate risks associated with product loading and receiving at terminals, as well as involving vessels of varying sizes. Shell Pilipinas fully supports all national and local policies focused on environmental protection and biodiversity conservation and the government's efforts to restore and safeguard critical habitats.

3-3, 306-3 Shell Pilipinas is dedicated to maintaining the highest standards of safety at its facilities by ensuring they are carefully designed, properly operated, and regularly inspected and maintained to prevent spills or leaks of hazardous substances that could harm the environment and surrounding communities. The Company invests in both advanced equipment and employee training to effectively respond to potential spills. The Company strives to meet both internal and government requirements, including mandatory training on accident prevention and oil spill response. Each terminal has a comprehensive oil spill contingency that identifies nearby protected areas with significant biodiversity and the response protocols for managing potential oil spill incidents. Oil spill response is integrated into Shell Pilipinas crisis management framework, ensuring that Company leaders are well-equipped to handle emergencies. Company-wide simulation exercises also enhance the Company's preparedness and response capabilities. Furthermore, Shell Pilipinas mitigates risk through fit-for-purpose infrastructure and equipment designed for spill prevention and preparedness. These include primary and secondary containment measures such as terminal bund walls and containment bunds. In the event of an incident, each facility is equipped with dedicated spill response tools to manage the situation effectively.

SPC is also a leader in resource circularity, working to minimise waste and promote the reuse of materials in sectors such as plastic, furniture, and textiles. By closing the loop on resource use, the Company reduces its dependence on finite materials, while simultaneously lessening environmental impacts. This approach is supported by rigorous solid and hazardous waste management systems, which ensure that waste is managed responsibly and in compliance with environmental standards.

This project also aligns with Shell's global aim to increase the recycled content in its packaging to 30% by 2030, while contributing to its 110-year legacy of sustainability in the Philippines.

This initiative promotes awareness and action both internally and externally, encouraging employees and partners to actively engage in reducing textile waste by upcycling it into useful and sustainable products. Collaborations with fashion schools like the College of St. Benilde, SOFA, and iAcademy emphasised sustainable design and HSSE-compliant practices in the fashion industry. content_text: Shell Pilipinas continues to prioritise diversity, equity & inclusion (DE&I) as an integral part of its operations and company culture. In 2024, Shell strengthened its commitment with initiatives designed to foster an inclusive environment where every individual is respected, supported, and given the opportunity to succeed. The 'DE&I in Action' campaign, launched in 2023, and continues its traction for 2024. The theme 'How are you showing up?' focused on driving deeper conversations within teams and encouraging practical actions to advance inclusion. Through a film series, online content, and structured leader-led discussions, employees explored how DE&I can be embedded in daily operations. To ensure measurable progress, Shell Pilipinas rolled out tools such as the Powering Lives DE&I Employee Dashboard, which tracks representation and progress against the Company's goals. The Self-ID program expanded to 23 countries, including the Philippines, enabling employees to voluntarily share information on disability, gender identity, and sexual orientation. This effort provides valuable data for shaping policies and improving workplace inclusivity. In the Philippines, Self-ID declarations showed that 1.5% of employees identified as persons with disabilities, 12% reported diverse gender identities, and 11.2% identified as part of the LGBTQIA+ community. Creating an accessible workplace remains a core focus. The Disability, Accessibility, and Inclusion Portal equips employees with resources to better understand and support diverse needs. The Workplace Accessibility Programme ensures all employees have the tools and physical adjustments needed to perform at their best, whether through adaptive technologies, ergonomic workstations, or accessibility software. Gender equity is another priority for Shell Pilipinas. Regular pay equity reviews confirm that the Company's gender pay gap remains below 1%, significantly outperforming global benchmarks. Tailored action plans for each business unit address gender imbalances, considering factors such as talent availability and regional goals. Employees are also encouraged to set DE&I goals that drive change at both team and organisational levels. Throughout 2024, Shell Pilipinas marked key observances such as International Women's Day, Pride Month, and the International Day of People with Disabilities. These events reaffirm the Company's commitment in creating an environment where everyone feels valued and supported.

3-3 Shell Pilipinas maintained a strong recruitment process in 2024, guided by its commitment to fairness, transparency, and strategic workforce planning. In 2024, the Company faced no significant challenges in hiring new talents, with most business streams achieving a 100% offer acceptance rate. This success reflects Shell Pilipinas' competitive offerings, strong corporate culture, and commitment to Safety and Well-being, Care, and DE&I. Such continues to attract highly qualified professionals across the broader industry. The recruitment process, led by HR, follows a standardised framework applied across all departments. This framework ensures equal opportunities for all candidates through the consistent broadcast of job openings, clear application guidance, and transparent announcements of successful hires. A key enhancement to the recruitment process, introduced in 2023 and carried forward into 2024, is the implementation of a more flexible rehiring policy. The minimum waiting period for former employees to become eligible for rehire was reduced to six months from their last day on payroll. This adjustment allows the Company to remain agile and competitive in a dynamic labour market, particularly during the energy transition and the evolving landscape of workforce dynamics, including the rising trend of 'boomerang workers,' employees who leave a company for various reasons and are rehired at a later date. To manage turnover and ensure business continuity, Shell Pilipinas conducts regular talent and succession planning activities across all business streams. These efforts identify and prepare employees for key roles, providing a robust internal talent pipeline. When necessary, the Company also draws talent from other Shell entities in the Philippines, ensuring that every position is filled with the right person at the right time.

Shell Pilipinas continues to be recognised as a top employer in the Philippines, earning accolades from LinkedIn, the Philippine Inquirer, Statista, and Prosple. To promote career opportunities at Shell, the Company actively engages with diverse audiences and age groups through various activities and job fairs nationwide.

3-3, 401-2 Employees are offered competitive benefits and remuneration packages as part of Shell's commitment to attracting and retaining top talent. Shell Pilipinas conducted a comprehensive review of its benefits package, finding that most offerings continue to exceed industry standards since 2022. This review resulted in the harmonisation of over 90% of benefits across all business units, ensuring consistency and fairness across the organisation. At Shell Pilipinas, compensation is built on three core principles: paying well, paying fairly, and rewarding performance. The Company's pay is positioned within the top 25% of competitors in the talent market. Shell's compensation philosophy focuses on 'total cash', which includes base salary, performance-based bonuses, and fixed allowances. The Company also offers greater flexibility in its healthcare plan, providing essential support for employees and their families, making it one of the best in the industry. To ensure satisfaction from our employees, the Company gathers feedback through the Shell People Survey, which consistently reflects high satisfaction with the Company's Total Rewards program, placing it above Shell's global standards. A recent benefits review revealed that more than 90% of offerings are above industry standards. For areas identified as needing improvement, Shell Pilipinas implemented enhancements, further harmonising its benefits package and ensuring alignment with employee needs and expectations. Shell continues to evolve its approach to work in response to the Future of Work trends, introducing a Future of Work Playbook that allows employees to adopt flexible work patterns while anchored to a specific work location. As hybrid work setups become the norm, Shell leverages advanced software and hardware tools, offering both onsite and virtual IT support to ensure a seamless experience for all employees. Moreover, the Company supports the wellbeing of its employees and their families. In 2024, it continued to implement its eight-week parental leave policy to include non-birthing parents, regardless of sex, gender, or marital status. This leave applies to new or adoptive parents, whether through birth, legal adoption, or surrogacy, reinforcing Shell's commitment to inclusion and non-discrimination.

On August 1, 2023, Shell Pilipinas' SHIFT Operations transitioned to a 12-hour shift schedule, streamlining processes and improving efficiency. The new structure replaced the previous 24/7 schedule of three 8-hour shifts, which required time-intensive handovers that often led to significant overtime. Developed through careful planning and collaboration with the team, including unionised staff and with Shell Health regional Human Factors Experts, wherein fatigue risks are assessed and mitigated, the new system incorporates handovers into the shift framework, reducing downtime and overtime hours. By 2024, the optimised shift schedule has enhanced operational efficiency while ensuring employees receive adequate rest and that fatigue risks are managed. This initiative reflects Shell Pilipinas' commitment to balancing productivity with employee well-being, setting a benchmark for thoughtful workplace improvements.

content_text: Recognising that optimal vision is essential for safe and effective work, the Real Estate unit of Shell Pilipinas launched the Eye Camp Programme: Sharp Vision for a Bright Mission on November 27 and December 9, 2024. This initiative reflects SPC's commitment to the health, safety, and well-being of its frontline workforce, including technicians, housekeepers, messengers, drivers, security guards, supervisors, and contractors. Inspired by a successful eye-testing event at the Shell Technology Centre in Bangalore, Christian Tagros, our Real Estate Regional Facilities Manager, led the campaign's replication in Manila. The programme provided free eye checkups, consultations on eye care, and subsidies for basic eyeglasses. Remarkably, 92 of 114 contractor staff from TFC and Tabangao offices participated; among them, 98.9% were identified as needing corrective eyewear, with 96.7% successfully receiving their prescribed glasses. The impact of the Eye Camp initiative goes beyond simply providing corrective eyewear; it is a powerful example of paying it forward and creating an endless ripple of care. Aileen 'Pau' Salazar, a food and beverage attendant, shared how receiving subsidised eyeglasses with anti-radiation features has transformed her work, allowing her to clearly read food labels and signages. Contractor driver Alvin Cena echoed this sentiment, emphasising how the clear vision he gained has significantly enhanced his driving safety, especially at night. This idea of care extending far beyond the immediate benefit is at the heart of SPC's approach, showing respect and care '..not just in board meetings with our colleagues and executives, but in our everyday actions toward our partners who make our lives easier day by day." His words reinforce that this initiative is not merely a business activity but a genuine commitment to enhance quality of life and workplace safety.

content_text: 403-3, 403-6 Shell Pilipinas goes beyond standard benefits like Health Maintenance Organisation (HMO) coverage, life insurance, and disability protection by offering additional programmes to promote employee well-being. The Employee Assistance Programme (EAP) provides free counselling services for employees and their dependents, ensuring access to mental health support when needed. The Resilience Programme is a self-paced learning tool designed to help employees develop coping mechanisms and strategies for managing stress and navigating challenging situations effectively. Additionally, the Nutrition Programme offers personalised nutritional assessments, including referrals to specialists when necessary, with nutrition counselling covered under the HMO plan for employees and their dependents. In 2024, Shell Pilipinas took a significant step to ensure equity across the organisation by harmonising 90% of its benefits. This initiative guarantees that all employees, regardless of their company affiliation, receive consistent and comprehensive support.

Shell Pilipinas is setting the benchmark for advocating employee well-being with the Global Mental Wellbeing Program (GMWP), as part of Shell's Powering Progress strategy. The programme, designed to enable our people to thrive, focuses on three core goals: promoting healthy behaviors, protecting a safe and healthy workplace, and ensuring access to quality care and support services. Launched nationwide on February 12, 2024, the GMWP began with the GMWP survey that engaged 71% of our workforce. The survey identified critical focus areas: resilience for promoting wellbeing, demand and control for protecting our work environment, and gaps in sleep, physical activity, and nutrition. In response, we introduced targeted interventions with measurable outcomes empowering employees to take immediate, actionable steps towards better health and collaborative growth. - ■ A self-paced Resilience Programme that equips teams with practical strategies to manage stress and navigate challenges. - ■ The Sleep Well Campaign, featuring initiatives like 'Pillow Talk' for team-based discussions on science-backed sleep strategies, highlighting the importance of restorative sleep, and 'Bedroom on Wheels,' a virtual reality experience of optimal sleep environments. - ■ The Move More Campaign, which emphasises even small physical activities through interactive 'Jumpstart' sessions and ergonomic solutions such as sit-stand desks and stationary bikes. - ■ The Eat Well campaign inspires mindful eating and effective meal planning through engaging activities such as 'Reality Bites", which explored strategies for healthier meals, and the 'Wellness Wagon', which offered fun games focused on healthy habits.

content_text: 3-3, 403-1, 403-2, 403-4, 403-5, 403-7 , EM-EP-320a.2 Protecting the health and safety of employees, contractors, and communities is a top priority at Shell Pilipinas. The Company's commitment is guided by its 'Goal Zero' ambitionaiming for zero fatalities and zero incidents across operations. This focus is built around three critical areas: personal safety, process safety, and transport safety. Clear standards apply not only to Shell employees but also to contractors and joint ventures under the Company's operational control, ensuring a consistent and comprehensive approach to safety. Shell's Health, Safety, Security, and Environment (HSSE) & Social Performance Control Framework is the foundation for identifying, assessing, and managing workplace hazards and risks. Regular audits and integrated assurance plans help evaluate the effectiveness of safety measures and management practices. The HSSE Tech Forum facilitates updates, discussions, and alignment with safety standards for contractors and suppliers operating on Shell sites. Employees and contractors are empowered to actively contribute to safety through initiatives such as incident reporting and near-miss analyses. Importantly, all staff are authorised to stop work if unsafe conditions are observed.

403-5 At the Company, workers are trained to assess the safety of their working environment. This includes identifying and managing occupational safety hazards and risks, with a particular focus on asset integrity. Employees ensure that assets are built to specific engineering standards and that the Shell Global Reliability and Integrity maintenance plan is followed. Operating integrity is also closely monitored to ensure compliance with safe operating procedures. Business leaders are ultimately accountable for both asset integrity and worker safety. Employees working in HSSE-related roles receive training in accordance with Shell's global requirements as well as local legislation. Members of the Shell Health Team undergo specific training, including the Awareness of Health Risk Assessment, Knowledge of HRA Training, and IT User Training. HSSE Audit Courses are also available through Shell Open University to further enhance expertise in safety practises. For disaster preparedness, the Health Rescue Team regularly conducts First Aid Training, Basic Life Support, and Advance Rescue Training in partnership with the Philippine Red Cross and local hospitals. Additionally, operators in large assets receive Shell Incident Management System 300 Training, while Oil Spill Regional Exercises are held to mitigate the risk of spills and leaks. Crisis Management Exercises are also conducted for Shell Pilipinas leaders to ensure readiness in the event of an emergency. Shell Pilipinas follows a Calamity Resiliency Manual, which outlines how employees will be accounted for and details instruction on delivering immediate and long-term relief to staff and their families during a disaster. Each business unit also has its own Emergency Response Plan to address specific risks and ensure swift, coordinated action in times of crisis.

content_text: 403-3, 403-6 Shell Pilipinas provides occupational health services aimed at eliminating hazards and minimising risks in the workplace. These services include medical evaluations to assess 'fitness to work' for employees assigned to mediumand high-risks tasks, an annual medical examination for all employees, and onsite clinics at major Shell sites, including TFC and SHIFT. Health Risk Assessments are also conducted to identify and mitigate potential health hazards in the work environment. To prevent work-related illnesses, the Company communicates the findings and recommendations from the Health Risk Assessment to employees, ensuring they are aware of potential risks and protective measures. These hazards may include issues related to office ergonomics (such as the use of ergonomic equipment), exposure to chemicals (like petroleum products), physical risks (such as noise), as well as biological and psychological hazards (including stress-related issues). By addressing these risks, Shell Pilipinas safeguards the well-being of its employees by fostering a safer and healthier work environment.

403-1, 403-2 The Company's primary tool in managing risks is outlined in its Hazards and Effects Management Process. To minimise potential hazards, Shell Pilipinas employs a multiplebarrier thinking method approach, which involves implementing both control and recovery barriers. These barriers work together to prevent hazards and mitigate the impact of any potential high-consequence events. Examples of control barriers include the permitto-work system and a Job Hazard Analysis, while recovery barriers, such as the Emergency Response procedure, are in place to manage any incidents should they occur. In 2024, several audits were conducted across business units to ensure compliance with global and regional HSSE standards, ensuring alignment with Shell's commitment to safety and risk management.

The 57th Shell National Students Art Competition is more than just an art contest-it is a testament to Shell Pilipinas' enduring support for Filipino artists and its commitment to sustaining a vibrant creative industry. The Board of Directors, Corporate Officers, and Management of SPC follow the Revised Manual on Corporate Governance (the 'Manual') and acknowledge that the Manual guides SPC in the attainment of its goals and targets. This Manual provides the practical requirements to explain details of Shell's General Business Principles and sustainable development, both of which govern how each of the Shell companies conducts its affairs. Shell Companies have core values of honesty, integrity, and respect for people. These underlying corporate values determine principles that we apply to all transactions, large or small, and drive the behaviour expected of every Shell Pilipinas employee in the conduct of its business at all times. This Manual is issued in compliance with the Philippines Securities and Exchange Commission (the 'Commission' or 'SEC') Memorandum Circular No. 19, Series of 2016, dated 22 November 2016, otherwise known as the Code of Corporate Governance for Publicly Listed Companies, to develop a strong corporate governance culture in line with recent developments in corporate governance (e.g. G20/OECD Principles of Corporate Governance, ASEAN Corporate Governance Scorecard). The Manual is aligned with the Shell General Business Principles.

To ensure adherence to corporate principles and best practices provided for in the Revised Manual on Corporate Governance, the Board of Directors designates a Chief Compliance Officer, who is not a member of the Board. He has direct reporting responsibilities to the Chairman of the Board but is primarily liable to SPC and its shareholders and not to the Chairman or President of SPC. The Chief Compliance Officer is a separate individual from the Corporate Secretary. The CCO performs the following duties and responsibilities: - a. In coordination with the Corporate Secretary, ensure proper onboarding of new directors such as providing orientation programmes on SPC's business, articles of incorporation, and by-laws, among others; - b. Monitor, review, evaluate, and ensure the compliance by SPC, its officers, and directors with the relevant laws, provisions, and requirements of this Manual, rules and regulations, and all governance issuances of regulatory agencies; - c. Appear before the Commission upon summons on similar matters that need to be clarified by the same in relation to the compliance with the Manual; - d. Determine violation/s of the Manual and recommend imposition of appropriate disciplinary action for violations thereof for further review and approval of the Board and the adoption of measures to prevent a repetition of the violations; - e. Ensure the integrity and accuracy of all documentary submissions to regulators; and - f. Collaborate with the Corporate Secretary and other departments to properly address compliance issues, which may be subject to investigation and subsequent litigation.

content_text: 2-14 It is the Board's responsibility to foster the long-term success of the Company and to sustain its competitiveness and profitability in a manner consistent with its corporate objectives and the best interest of its stockholders and other stakeholders. The Board oversees the development of, formulates and approves the Company vision, mission, strategic objectives, business objectives and strategy, policies, and procedures that guide its activities, including the means to effectively monitor management's performance. The Company also monitors their implementation, in order to sustain SPC's longterm viability and strength. The Board has a Board Charter that defines its roles, responsibilities, and accountabilities in carrying out its fiduciary duties.

A director's office is one of trust and confidence. A director acts in the best interest of SPC in a manner characterised by transparency, accountability, and fairness. He also exercises leadership, prudence, and integrity in directing SPC towards sustained progress. A director acts on a fully informed basis, in good faith, with due diligence and care, and in the best interest of the Company and all shareholders and other stakeholders.

The Board is headed by a competent and qualified Chairman. To avoid conflict or a split board and to foster an appropriate balance of power, increased accountability, and better capacity for independent decision-making, the Chairman of the Board is a separate person from the CEO. The duties and responsibilities of the Chairman in relation to the Board include, among others, the following: - a. Makes certain that the meeting agenda focuses on strategic matters, including the overall risk appetite of the Company, considering the developments in the business and regulatory environments, key governance concerns, and contentious issues that will significantly affect operations; - b. Guarantees that the Board receives accurate, timely, relevant, insightful, concise, and clear information to enable it to make sound decisions; - c. Facilitates discussions on key issues by fostering an environment conducive to constructive debate and leveraging the skills and expertise of individual directors; - d. Ensures that the Board sufficiently challenges and inquiries into reports submitted and representations made by Management; - e. Assures the availability of proper orientation for first-time directors and continuing training opportunities for all directors; - f. Makes sure that the performance of the Board is evaluated at least once a year and discussed or followed up on; - g. Ensures that the meetings of the Board are held in accordance with the by-laws or as the Chairman may deem necessary; - h. Supervises the preparation of the agenda of the meeting in coordination with the Corporate Secretary, taking into consideration the suggestions of the CEO, Management, and the Directors; and - i. Maintains qualitative and timely lines of communication and information between the Board and Management.

The duties and responsibilities of the CEO include, among others, the following: - a. Determines the Company's strategic direction and formulates and implements its strategic plan on the direction of the business; - b. Communicates and implements the Company's vision, mission, values, and overall strategy and promotes any organisation or stakeholder change in relation to the same; - c. Oversees the operations of the Company and manages human and financial resources in accordance with the strategic plan; - d. Has a good working knowledge of the Company's industry and market and keeps up-to-date with its core business purpose; - e. Directs, evaluates, and guides the work of the key officers of the Company; - f. Manages the Company's resources prudently and ensures a proper balance of the same; - g. Provides the Board with timely information and interfaces between the Board and the employees; - h. Builds the corporate culture and motivates the employees of the Company; and - i. Serves as the link between internal operations and external stakeholders.

Performance self-assessments are annually conducted for the Board, individual members of the Board, Committees, and the Management. Results are tabulated and presented by the Corporate Governance Committee to the Board. At the close of every year, business managers sign off on their respective Business Assurance Letters, addressed to the President and CEO, assuring that there have been no incidents of non-compliance or breaches of trust. Likewise, both the President and Chief Executive Officer and the Corporate Audit and Assurance Manager issue an attestation on the effectiveness of internal controls.

3-3 Shell Pilipinas has risk management policies to ensure that the business operates in the most optimal way to achieve its goals as set out in the Powering Progress strategy. In line with this, SPC's Risk Management Policy explicitly states that management is responsible for implementing, operating, and monitoring the system of internal control, which is designed to provide reasonable but not absolute assurance of achieving business objectives. The approach to internal control includes several general and specific risk management processes and policies. The primary control mechanisms are self-appraisal processes in combination with strict accountability for results. Visit this link to learn more about how Shell Pilipinas manages enterprise risk.

Shell Pilipinas is investing in technologies to protect the business and Information Technology (IT) landscape to prevent cyber security incidents from happening. The Company adopts the Line of Defense model, which is a market standard risk management model. Shell also has a robust global IT incident reporting process and mechanism. Moreover, the Company is constantly building its recovery readiness capabilities to enable the rapid recovery from any incident and thrive in new circumstances after the event has passed. Additionally, Shell cyber defence experts assess potentially damaging cyber threats and identify and remediate system vulnerabilities, based on threat intelligence and network scanning data. They also continuously monitor the Shell IT network for patterns of abnormal behaviour and when an incident is detected, assess the impact, and take action to contain and remediate the issue. Cyber actors, attack methods and targets are evolving and becoming more sophisticated. Given this, Shell Pilipinas has the Think Secure Programme, which trains its staff members on Cyber Fundamentals-a guideline for employees. In 2024, there were no cybersecurity breaches in Shell Pilipinas. Shell Pilipinas aims to protect and manage personal data in a professional, lawful, and ethical manner. Personal data is any information, on a physical document or in electronic form, relating to an identified or identifiable individual. Shell's Ethics and Compliance Manual instructs how the Company must implement Group requirements relating to compliance with Data Privacy laws. Also, SPC is governed by Shell's Binding Corporate Rules (BCR), which reflects the EU's General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR), as well as other requirements where the local law is stricter than the BCR. There have been no data privacy-related incidents noted in 2024.

March 18, 2025 The Board Audit and Risk Oversight Committee ("Committee") Shell Pilipinas Corporation The Corporate Assurance and Audit Department (CAAD) had reviewed the adequacy and effectiveness of the overall internal control system of Shell Pilipinas Corporation (SPC or Company) for the year ended December 31, 2024. The review covered all material controls, including financial, operational, and compliance controls. The review approach was based on the results of the SPC Management Business Assurance Letter (BAL) process and the various assurance activities undertaken within the Company for the year ended December 31, 2024. Management's response to controls self-assessment, in line with the BAL process, was either a "qualification", "commentary", or "no issue". Responses to the Business Assurance Letter were validated by CAAD in conjunction with the results of the various assurance activities, which were risk-based and were not intended to cover all areas of SPC nor all possible risks. The risk-based assurance plan was approved by, and the results were reported to the Committee. CAAD activities conform with the International Standards for the Professional Practice of Internal Auditing and are continuously evaluated through internal and external assessments. Based on the results of controls self-assessments, risk-based assurance reviews, and the reliance on the work of Sycip, Gorres, Velayo & Co. (SGV & Co.), the Company's external auditor, on their audit of the Company's December 31, 2024 financial statements, we conclude that, to the best of our knowledge and confidence, SPC's system of internal control is generally adequate and effective.
